clue.text: Frolic from island about most of Channel

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from an island to cross most of the English Channel for fun.

explanation.definitionFit: To skylark is to play about mischievously, a synonym of frolic.

explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist Frank G. Slaughter wrote Countdown, so he is its creator.

Jennifer Sommersby's 2018 young-adult fantasy set in a travelling circus

explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is deceptive skill, so the word means trickery or craftiness; it is also the title of Sommersby's circus book.

clue.text: Start to go on about one heartless Athenian, or Spartan

clue.text: Goldfinger — one for all to see at the cinema, endlessly sumptuous

taken as written

clue.text: Where Sidney Lanier wrote ast part of sonnet about mother and father

clue.text: Timeless mystic Alpine arts and crafts

clue.text: Where Berenson was born, in broken-down Italian hut mostly

mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: An art critic grew up in a dilapidated Italian hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the T of 'hut', and 'broken-down' rearranges ITALIAN with HU. Bernard Berenson, the art historian of the Italian Renaissance, was born near Vilnius.
explanation.definitionFit: Berenson was born in 1865 in the Baltic country whose capital is Vilnius.

clue.text: Author's nod to Gertrude

parts.note: Gertrude Stein was an American modernist writer
a beck is a nod or gesture of command, as in at someone's beck and call

explanation.walkthrough: 'Author's' gives the definition, its 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American novelist of The Grapes of Wrath.

clue.text: Dances get going in parties at Baltic capital

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the start-up word inside the parties; 'at' is only a link joining the Latvian capital to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively old Provençal dance for couples, so rigadoons are dances.

clue.text: Left with mixed-up girl? Not a great Shakespearean character

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' with 'great' removes G from GIRL, and 'mixed-up' turns IRL into RIL.

clue.text: Mass in which revised sonnet hasn't succeeded

explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't succeeded' takes S from SONNET, and 'revised' rearranges ONNET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonne is a metric unit of weight, a thousand kilograms, so a measure of mass.
